title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The notes build discrete models (groupoids I_J to IV_J) of the fundamental groupoid of P^1 minus {0,1,∞}. The base points are the three 'tangential' points Q_i and two points P_± in the upper and lower half-planes. The arcs are ã_i^ω (ω ∈ {+,-}, the half-planes). The symmetry group is G_J = S_3 × {1,τ}, where τ is complex conjugation swapping the half-planes. Grothendieck parametrizes automorphisms u of the groupoid III_J that fix the vertices and commute with S_3. Each such u is given by one element α̃ of the profinite group π̂_{0,3} = π̂_1(P^1 − 3 points). It must satisfy the cyclic relation (26), and u acts on arcs by u(ã) = ψ(α̃)ã. When α̃ comes from a pair (y, γ) via (27), α̃ = y^{-1} l_0^γ ε_0(y), the previous page computes α̃ ε_0(α̃) l_0 = y^{-1} l_0^p y with p = 2γ+1.

This page, step 1. Transport everything to one vertex group π(Q_{ω'i}) ≅ π_{0,3} via the path ψ, and identify the loop λ̃_i^ω with l_0. Then u(l_0) = y^{-1} l_0^p y. In modern language: the automorphism sends a generator of local inertia to a conjugate of its p-th power, with p = 2γ+1 playing the role of the cyclotomic character λ = 2m+1. This is exactly the shape σ(x) = f^{-1} x^λ f of the Ihara/Drinfeld–GT description, with y in the role of f and γ in the role of m.

Step 2: the symmetry τ. Conjugating u by the antiholomorphic involution τ, u ↦ τ(u) = τuτ, changes the parameter by (31): α̃' = ε_0 τ_∞(α̃^{-1}) = σ̃_0(α̃^{-1}). Here σ̃_i = σ_i τ_i are the orientation-reversing 'reflections'. They generate a group S̃_3 ≅ S_3, the stabilizer of P_+ in S_3 × {1,τ}, which maps canonically to Aut π̂_{0,3}. Its action is σ̃_i(l_i) = l_i^{-1} and σ̃_i(l_j) = l_k^{-1}, where {i,j,k} = {0,1,∞}.

Step 3: the twisted action. S̃_3 contains the rotation group S̃_3^+ = {1, ρ, ρ^2} with index 2, and the odd elements conjugate ρ to ρ^{-1}. Hence S̃_3 acts on the solution set V of the 3-cycle equation x ρ^{-1}(x) ρ^{-2}(x) = 1 by the twisted rule (32): θ_g x = g(x)^{sg(g)}, where sg(g) = ±1 according to orientation. Formula (33) then reads α̃' = θ_{σ̃_0}(α̃).

So conjugation by complex conjugation acts on Grothendieck's parameter space through an explicit affine-type action of S_3 on the solutions of the 'hexagon' relation. Purpose: to determine which solutions α̃ correspond to τ-equivariant (real) automorphisms, and to compute how the Galois parameters of σ and cσc are related. This is a precursor to the GT-relations of Drinfeld and Ihara.
errors: No mathematical error found. Check of (32): if x ∈ V and g is odd, apply g to the equation to get gx · ρ(gx) · ρ^2(gx) = 1, using gρ^{-1} = ρg. Inverting and using ρ^3 = 1 shows (gx)^{-1} ∈ V. The composition rule θ_gθ_h = θ_{gh} also holds, so (32) is a genuine action.

Minor imprecision: the subgroup is written {1, ρ^{-1}, ρ^{-2}}, which is the same set as {1, ρ, ρ^2}. The identification S̃_3 → π̃_{0,3} is labelled 'homomorphisme canonique'; it should be read as a map into Aut(π_{0,3}), or into the extended groupoid.

ideas.what: Galois-type automorphism sends inertia generator l_0 to y^{-1} l_0^p y with p = 2γ+1 (odd exponent parametrized as 2m+1)
ideas.modern_name: Parametrization of GT / Ihara action σ(x) = x^λ, σ(y) = f^{-1} y^λ f with m = (λ−1)/2
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme alludes to the 'Lego' description of the Galois action via genus 0 with 3 or 4 points, but gives no formulas

ideas.what: Cyclic equation x ρ^{-1}(x) ρ^{-2}(x) = 1 for the twisted element α̃ = y^{-1} l_0^γ ε_0(y)
ideas.modern_name: Hexagon (3-cycle) relation of GT: f(z,x) z^m f(y,z) y^m f(x,y) x^m = 1

ideas.what: Group S̃_3 of orientation-reversing symmetries (stabilizer of P_+ in S_3 × {complex conjugation}) and its twisted action θ_g x = g(x)^{sg(g)} on the solution set of the hexagon equation; formula for conjugation of u by τ
ideas.modern_name: Action of complex conjugation / extended symmetries on GT parameters (relation of (λ,f) for σ and cσc; element (−1,1) of GT)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (GT contains (−1,1)); Ihara; Lochak–Schneps work on the structure of GT

missed.claim: Explicit pre-Drinfeld (c. 1978–81) derivation of the hexagon-type equation together with a sign-twisted S_3-action on its solution set. This action encodes conjugation by the antiholomorphic involution and complements the 2-cycle relation. It gives documentary evidence that Grothendieck had the 3-cycle relation and the λ = 2m+1 parametrization in explicit form.
missed.quote: il s'ensuit que S̃_3 opère sur V ensemble des solutions x de l'équation x ρ^{-1}(x) ρ^{-2}(x) = 1 par θ_g x = g·x^{sg(g)}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority and documentation of Grothendieck's anticipation of GT. The twisted action itself is mathematically routine and implicit in later work.

missed.claim: Marginal note proposing that the conjugacy statement u(l_0) ~ l_0^p generalizes to other elements or loops stabilized by elements of S̃_3. The note is illegible in part and left undeveloped.
missed.quote: NB Ce dernier point se généralise (?) pour ... stabilisateurs ...
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor; it corresponds to the known fact that all three inertia generators are sent to conjugates of their λ-th powers.

deep.surprise_reason: It is already known in broad terms that Grothendieck anticipated GT. This page shows the explicit 3-cycle equation, the parametrization p = 2γ+1, and a clean twisted S_3-action for the complex-conjugation symmetry. These are notable archival details but contain no mathematics absent from the post-1990 literature.
